newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Apr 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Apr 7.

text.p: New Zealand Rugby Union was standing by its man after Wellington Hurricanes winger Roger Randle was charged in Durban, South Africa with rape. Hurricanes manager Tony Bedford posted bail of 5000 rand (NZ$1600) for Randle, 22, who is alleged to have raped a 31-year-old woman. Page 1

Labour's male vote declined at the last election partly because of a "residual resistance to a female leader", party deputy leader Michael Cullen said at the weekend. Cullen said the party needed to consider ways to boost its support among male voters after polling revealed that 60 percent of Labour voters at the election were women. Page 1.

Conservation Minister Nick Smith has indicated state-owned enterprise Timberlands might lose its right to log 7,000 hectares of native Buller forest. Under a 1986 deal negotiated between the government, conservationists, local authorities and the logging industry, Timberlands is allowed to log the forest near Charleston till 2006.

The release of a report on liquor laws is likely to be more than a week away, a Justice Minister spokesman said. The report follows a review of the laws governing alcohol sales by a committee headed by former chief ombudsman Sir John Robertson. Page 2.

The Labour Party's constitution was ignored when the manifesto was written for the last election, with much of it compiled by MPs without consulting other party members, list MP Marian Hobbs said at the weekend. Page 2.

The Cabinet may decide today whether to join an appeal against a district court ruling that Maoris could in some circumstances fish for trout without a licence. Judge Andrew Becroft ruled last month that Maoris fishing in traditional areas with the approval of appropriate authorities and with an eye to conservation limits did not need a licence. Page 2.

New Zealand's success in promoting the freeing-up of capital flows among members of the Asia-Pacific Economic Forum was a highlight for Treasurer Winston Peters at the Apec finance ministers' meeting in the Philippines. Peters, speaking from Cebu, said there had been much interest in how the government was operating as a coalition. Page 2.

The Health Ministry is writing to food manufacturers asking if any of their products contain genetically-modified organisms. The ministry is unable to tell the public what products in New Zealand, if any, have been created using gene technology. Page 3.

Trans Tasman Properties will register the prospectus for a proposed $310 million split-off of its Australian portfolio on Tuesday and plans to explain the finer details of the deal to prospective New Zealand investors at the end of the week. Page 11.
